title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was reused by both arms; downstream deterministic validation and at‑most‑one permitted repair (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms that could create paired differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] (reported as a descriptive summary). Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total hosted model calls recorded = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar as the prespecified confirmatory outcome, label any one‑sided McNemar as exploratory/post‑hoc, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, very high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations promises reduced manual effort but raises safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that degrade correctness for code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates purely downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our research question is: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate, to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus a single allowed repair call (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)? The design intentionally isolates downstream interventions so that any paired difference is attributable to deterministic validation decisions and the permitted repair call rather than to first‑pass generation differences, prompt engineering, or sampling variance.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from a synthetic stress corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Transparent execution accounting and artifacted validator traces showing how downstream validation and a bounded repair budget produced the observed paired differences. (3) A disciplined statistical interpretation that treats the exact two‑sided McNemar as the preregistered confirmatory test and labels all non‑prespecified directional tests or exploratory summaries accordingly, with explicit discussion of power and baseline‑prevalence effects on detectability.
sections.related_work:
LLM reliability work documents hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and generation failure modes that affect structured outputs and code generation [2],[3]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning improve executable rates in other structured domains, but transfer to NetOps depends on validator fidelity and topology heterogeneity [4]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system papers propose verifier‑assisted repair, digital twins, and governance/proof‑carrying mechanisms to mitigate automation risk; these offer prototypes and architectural arguments emphasizing that operational reliability depends on validator coverage and external protocol enforcement rather than on any single model alone [5],[6].

Our study complements this literature by preregistering a paired comparison whose estimand isolates the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single limited repair call when the initial candidate is held constant across conditions. This isolation avoids conflating downstream interventions with first‑pass prompt/decoding differences and clarifies what the guarded pipeline actually achieved under the executed semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered (identifier: cand‑003‑stud‑001) and frozen prior to any hosted‑model calls. Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministically drawn from a synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries included a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe. The preregistration document and execution artifacts are archived with the run.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and guarded episodes begin from the identical sampled initial candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject the candidate via deterministic validation and may invoke at most one allowed repair call. Consequently, paired outcome differences can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and the permitted repair. The experiment therefore does not measure effects of independent first‑pass generations, alternative prompts, constrained decoding arms, or sampling variance — those were not part of the frozen experiment.

Model and runtime configuration. The declared provider/model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and the orchestration/validator layer was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the digital‑twin validator. The archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The deterministic validator enforces workflow policies, required command presence and order, protected‑field noninterference, and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest.

Task corpus and scoring. Tasks were selected deterministically per the preregistered selection rule to produce exactly 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest included initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard or extreme). The validator compared parsed candidate command sequences against manifest constraints in a deterministic digital‑twin emulator and emitted structured validator traces archived per episode. Scoring used full_intent_constraint_validation producing a binary validity outcome used by the paired analysis.

Execution accounting and missingness rules. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness treatments (primary analysis uses complete_pair_primary). The executor recorded model calls and repair events; all missingness reasons and any deviations were archived. No human adjudication or manual imputation occurred.
sections.results:
Execution summary. The preregistered run completed all planned paired episodes (complete_pairs = 1000). The provider audit recorded the shared initial generation stage for every task and five repair-stage invocations; total hosted model calls recorded = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). No episodes were excluded post‑hoc and no failed episodes were recorded under the preregistered execution accounting.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05, so the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Confirmatory vs descriptive summaries (inferential hierarchy). By prerogative of the frozen preregistration, the exact two‑sided McNemar is the confirmatory analysis and is the primary inferential statement (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is a preregistered descriptive summary and yields [0.001, 0.01]; this CI excludes zero because bootstrap percentiles can be sensitive to extremely sparse discordant counts and should be treated as descriptive here. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) yields p = 0.03125; because a directional test was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is reported explicitly as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not change the preregistered confirmatory conclusion. These points constitute the preregistered inferential hierarchy and were requested and clarified per the peer review.

Repair diagnostics and representative cases. Five validator‑triggered repairs were observed; archived episode traces show repairs invoked to correct required_sequence violations or protected‑field touches that the deterministic validator detected. Representative discordant pairs (five pair IDs) and their high‑level failure reasons are archived in the evidence bundle; they illustrate the narrow set of failure modes the repair budget addressed. Detailed per‑episode raw responses and validator traces are archived and referenced by the execution manifest.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation given observed baseline prevalence. The preregistered power plan assumed a substantially lower baseline success rate (≈0.60) and targeted a 0.15 absolute improvement; the observed baseline (0.995) is far higher than that assumption and therefore produced very few discordant pairs, reducing power for the exact paired test. This mismatch is the principal reason a small absolute guarded improvement (0.005) did not reach two‑sided statistical significance under the preregistered test. Hence, failure to reject the null at α = 0.05 should be interpreted in the context of limited discordant counts rather than as conclusive evidence of no practical benefit in other regimes with higher baseline failure rates.

Mechanistic implications within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both arms began from the same sampled candidate, the observed n10 = 5 discordant successes are attributable only to deterministic validator decisions and the single allowed repair calls; the guarded pipeline did not benefit from independent first‑pass sampling or alternative prompts in this design. The small number of repairs shows that when baseline candidate validity is already high, downstream repair budget produces few opportunities to improve outcomes. Distinguishing whether high baseline validity derives from the generator, the synthetic corpus, or validator permissiveness requires follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity. Construct validity depends on validator rule coverage: omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity is strengthened by shared_initial_candidate semantics but at the cost of not measuring prompt/decoding interventions. External validity is limited by a single model (gpt‑5‑mini), a synthetic corpus, and a deterministic emulator validator. Conclusion validity is reduced by sparse discordant counts and the consequent discrete boundary behavior of exact paired tests.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired study isolating downstream effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) over a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total recorded model calls = 1005. The preregistered exact McNemar is the confirmatory inferential statement; bootstrap summaries and any directional tests are descriptive or exploratory and are reported as such. Artifacted traces show that verifier‑guided repair can prevent some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend strongly on baseline failure prevalence, validator coverage, and repair budget. Follow‑ups should preregister designs targeted at regimes with higher baseline failure rates, vary repair budgets, expand validator rule sets and topology heterogeneity, and evaluate multiple model families to establish generality.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
